sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Everything we've designed so far makes KoreVity incredibly powerful.

sections.title: Phase 17 is what makes it unstoppable.

paragraphs: Don't build the Developer Portal as documentation.
Build it as a Developer Operating System.

A developer should be able to spend their entire day inside the portal—from reading documentation to building, testing, deploying, publishing, and monitoring their extensions—without leaving the platform.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next component should be Enterprise SDK.
The SDK is the foundation that every extension, application, plugin, workflow, AI agent, and marketplace solution will rely on.
If the Developer Portal is the front door, the Enterprise SDK is the toolbox that empowers developers to build the future of the KoreVity ecosystem.
Now we're building what every great platform has:
The SDK determines whether developers love your platform or fight against it.
A great SDK makes difficult things simple.
A poor SDK makes simple things difficult.
For KoreVity, the SDK must feel like building with Lego blocks, not wiring a data center.

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: Developers should think about solving business problems.

sections.title: The Enterprise SDK is the official developer toolkit that provides secure, versioned, type-safe, and extensible access to every KoreVity capability, enabling developers to build applications, AI agents, workflows, extensions, integrations, and marketplace solutions using consistent APIs and development patterns.
Engineering Summary
paragraphs: The SDK becomes the standard way to build on KoreVity.

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: Instead of one massive SDK, build a Composable SDK.

Instead of exposing a fixed API surface, the SDK dynamically understands the capabilities available in the connected enterprise.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next component should be Extension Framework.

If the SDK gives developers tools and the CLI gives them speed, the Extension Framework gives them the power to safely extend every part of the KoreVity platform without modifying the core itself.

Everything before this was preparing for it.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next component should be Plugin Runtime.
The Extension Framework defines what extensions are.
The Plugin Runtime defines how they actually execute.

This runtime is what allows hundreds—or even thousands—of independently developed extensions to run safely inside the same enterprise platform without compromising stability, security, or performance.
The Extension Framework defines the contract.
The Plugin Runtime is the engine that actually runs everything.

It will allow partners and customers to extend KoreVity's automation capabilities just as easily as they extend its applications, making workflows a first-class development artifact rather than a fixed platform feature.

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: Trust should be earned through measurable validation.
Certification is not a marketing badge.
It is objective proof that a solution meets enterprise standards.

sections.title: The Certification Platform is the enterprise validation and accreditation framework responsible for automatically and manually evaluating applications, AI agents, workflows, extensions, integrations, packages, and marketplace solutions against KoreVity quality, security, performance, compliance, accessibility, and operational standards before and throughout their lifecycle.
Engineering Summary
paragraphs: Certification becomes an ongoing engineering process, not a one-time review.

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: Don't treat certification as a checklist.
Every marketplace asset receives a continuously updated trust profile instead of a static certification.
As new vulnerabilities, platform versions, or AI evaluation methods emerge, the trust profile evolves automatically.
This creates a living measure of software quality rather than a point-in-time approval.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would implement a Certification Evidence Graph.
Instead of a simple "Certified" badge, every certification is backed by traceable evidence.
Enterprise customers can inspect why a solution is trusted, while publishers receive precise guidance on improving weak areas.
This turns certification into a transparent, data-driven trust model.

sections.title: First Principle
paragraphs: Buying enterprise software should feel like installing a business capability.
A marketplace should deliver complete enterprise solutions.

sections.title: Enterprise Marketplace Integration is the unified ecosystem orchestration platform that seamlessly connects marketplace assets, package management, deployment, licensing, billing, security, certification, governance, AI agents, workflows, enterprise applications, and organizational administration into a single enterprise software acquisition and lifecycle experience.
Engineering Summary
paragraphs: The marketplace becomes an integrated enterprise delivery platform.

sections.title: 🏛️ The Biggest Architectural Insight of Phase 17
paragraphs: Build an Enterprise Development Operating System.
Everything a developer, partner, or enterprise needs exists inside one cohesive ecosystem.
One operating system for enterprise software innovation.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would implement an Enterprise Capability Graph.
Instead of installing isolated software, organizations install a complete business capability.
For example, "Procurement" or "Customer Success" becomes a graph of interconnected assets that the platform understands as a single deployable unit.
This dramatically simplifies deployment, upgrades, governance, and lifecycle management.
